definition: Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP) is a technique for training a pair of neural network models, one for image understanding and one for text understanding, using a contrastive objective.
details: This method has enabled broad applications across multiple domains, including cross-modal retrieval, text-to-image generation, and aesthetic ranking.
story: Picture walking through a crowd and instantly picking out a familiar face without reading a single name tag. Think of it this way: Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP) is a technique for training a pair of neural network models, one for image understanding and one for text understanding, using a contrastive objective. And here is the clever part: This method has enabled broad applications across multiple domains, including cross-modal retrieval, text-to-image generation, and aesthetic ranking. Sight, for a machine, is a long climb from raw light to a name. And that is Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training — giving a machine the gift of sight.
